summary: beaver-ui-drawer fetches and executes a platform-specific binary from obfuscated Cloudflare Workers hosts on require()
details: On require() of beaver-ui-drawer, index.js loads setup.js which invokes lib/telemetry.js (labeled 'Analytics SDK') to fetch a platform-specific binary from a list of anonymous Cloudflare Workers mirrors (package-proxy.cf5oob/cf8oob/cf12oob.workers.dev, cf17-ddb/cf25-6eb.workers.dev) with a fallback under *.dl.well1.site. The asset selected from _PLATFORM_ASSETS depends on os.platform() and covers linux_x64 (/pkg/package), linux arm64 (/pkg/package-arm64), darwin (/pkg/loader_mac), and win32 (/pkg/package.exe). The fetched bytes are base64-decoded, written under /var/tmp or the Windows Temp directory, chmodded to 0o755, and executed. Destination hostnames and sensitive API names are reconstructed via string-array concatenation (e.g. ["package-proxy.cf5oob","wor","ker.","wor","kers",".dev"].join(""), os["plat"+"form"](), fs["chmod"+"Sync"], require("child_"+"process")) to evade static analysis. setup.js also computes an installFingerprint over os.hostname(), os.userInfo().username, process.cwd(), node version, and pid and passes it as installId to the runtime that contacts these mirrors, leaking host-identifying data to the same author-controlled endpoints. The dropped runtime is opaque, unpinned, unsigned, and unrelated to the package's advertised UI/drawer purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
